messages.author: 3b469b246ecd3a5b
messages.subject: quantile smoothing and formula
parts:
I am confused about mapping variables to scales or formulas in general
or most likely both.

I'll use the mpg dataset as an example.

The following works fine and does what I expect: [examples done in
ggplot2 0.8.6 ]

p <- qplot(x=hwy, y=displ, data = mpg)
p + stat_quantile(formula = y ~ log(x))

It produces a quantile smoothed curve that is done on the log of
displ. But in my real dataset I have dollars on the y axis and what I
really want would be the equivalent of the following:

p <- qplot(x=hwy, y=displ, data = mpg)
p + stat_quantile(formula = log(y) ~ x)

This does the quantile smoothing that I expect, but it plots the
quantile lines as though the scale values were log(y) rather than y,
which is not what I want. I want the y axis to remain as hwy (in this
example) and to have the y value for the smoothing converted back from
log(hwy) into hwy.

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: quantile smoothing and formula
parts:
Hi John,

The problem is that R has no idea what the inverse transformation is.
For this case, I'd suggest fitting the model yourself and adding the
lines manually.

Hadley

messages.subject: Re: quantile smoothing and formula
parts:
Thanks, Hadley.

I had figured out that I needed to use predict() and geom_line(). I
also used stat_function() and included use of predict() inside the
function I passed to stat_function().

I am still finding that my head is not completely clear about aes()
and mapping. I am getting better about understanding when I can just
do colour="red" and when I have to do colour=I("red"), for example.
And when do I need to use aes(). I feel like I need to sit down and
work through some of the examples in the book. I read the book last
year as a PDF and I've been going through the print version again.
It's a short book, but it's remarkable how dense it is. There's a lot
in that small book. The manual at the web site helps a lot. I was
looking at an example by baptiste in which he was actually using
layer(). I should try to do some examples where I do the identical
plot via ggplot and layer and geom compared with qplot and geom.


--John

messages.subject: Re: quantile smoothing and formula
parts:
> I am still finding that my head is not completely clear about aes()
> and mapping.  I am getting better about understanding when I can just
> do colour="red" and when I have to do colour=I("red"), for example.

This is a difference between using qplot and adding layers by hand:

qplot(mpg, wt, data = mtcars, colour = "red")
ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt, colour = "red")) + geom_point()

qplot(mpg, wt, data = mtcars, colour = I("red"))
ggplot(mtcars, aes(mpg, wt), colour = "red") + geom_point()

Using I() in qplot basically tells ggplot to treat it as a parameter
to the layer instead of as an aesthetic. Does that help?
